plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Literacy, Years 5 and 6: completing and editing a persuasive text independently, assessed by the Term 4 writing CAT
plan.shape: assessment day: a quick where-am-I check, one check of what a conclusion must do, then protected writing and a timed read-aloud check before hand-in
plan.criticalFeature: the conclusion restates the position and sells it, with no new reason
decisionPoints: the fingers check at the start: how many parts are written?
the conclusion check: which ending does its job?
the 10-minute warning: is every student reading their piece against the checklist?
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Introduction claims, body paragraphs prove, conclusion sells.
plan.catchUp: Away yesterday? Give them the Plan Template (it has the questions and ideas), the full 40 minutes, and catch-up time for the rest; note it on the Elastik upload.

studentTools: Each student's Elastik pages from Session 1
Writer's notebooks or Plan Templates with yesterday's plan
Class copies of The Last Bear, for ideas only
routineIcons: Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: The writing placemat slide on the TV for the whole writing time
Write the hand-in time on the board, and the 10-minute check time
Thursday afternoon: upload the Elastik pages. Hand back each student's pages once theirs show as uploaded; an absentee's stay with you until their catch-up is uploaded.

slides.notes: Open the session: today students finish their CAT draft, check it and hand it in.
No printed sheets today: hand back each student's own Elastik pages. Keep a spare from the same Elastik task only to replace a spoilt page.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to finish and check a persuasive piece so it shows our best independent writing.
successCriteria: I can finish my body paragraphs with a reason, evidence and an explanation.
I can write a conclusion that restates my position and ends with a strong last line.
I can read my writing aloud quietly and fix what I find.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Today your piece gets finished, checked and handed in.
SAY: Let's read the I can lines together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three... one, two, three.
SAY: Finishing your body paragraphs is where everyone starts.
A conclusion that sells it is today's big goal.
notes.prep: SC1 and SC2 are the rest of the draft; SC3 is the checklist at the end. Keep it brisk: 1 minute.
notes.tag: [LI and SC | Planning made visible | HITS 1]

slides.title: Where are you up to?
slides.prompt: Show me the last part you finished.

beats: SAY: Find where you stopped yesterday on your Elastik pages.
ASK: Which is the last part you finished?
10 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest, voices off... show me.
EXPECT: 2, 3 or 4 for most
SCAN the fingers. Note anyone on 0 or 1.
80%+ on 2 or more -> move on.
Less -> same timing for everyone; note names beside the draft. Re-ask at 25.
SAY: Now quietly read your plan and your last paragraph.
That's how you pick up the thread.
trap: starting a new paragraph without rereading.
Fix: student reads their plan, then their last paragraph.
notes.prep: The fingers show who may not reach the conclusion; everyone gets the same time. 2 minutes.

slides.title: Which conclusion does its job?
slides.prompt: Question: Should our school have a music room?

options.text: In conclusion, music is fun. A music room could also have a stage for assemblies!
options.misconception: adds a new reason in the conclusion instead of summing up

options.text: Our school needs a music room. It builds confidence, teamwork and joy, so please sign our petition this week.
Thank you for reading my writing about music. I hope you liked it.
options.misconception: ends politely but never restates the position or asks the reader to act

notes.answer: B - it restates, sums up and ends with a call to action
beats: SAY: Before you write, let's check what a conclusion has to do.
Read all three in your head.
ASK: Which conclusion does its job?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> cold call one B: What's wrong with A? Then reveal.
Less -> point to Sell it on the placemat, read its four lines, re-ask.
trap: choosing A because it sounds exciting.
Fix: student finds the new idea in A, the stage, and says why it doesn't belong.
notes.prep: The decision point before release. A new idea in the ending caps the Text Structure row (rubric: no new ideas). Off-topic on purpose.

slides.title: Your turn: finish, then check
slides.task: Work on your own on your Elastik pages. Finish your piece, then check it.
steps: Write your conclusion: answer the question again and sell it.
Read it aloud quietly and check it against the CAT checklist.
slides.where: Elastik pages, with your plan beside you
slides.visualLabel: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it.
slides.extendedTask: the persuasive CAT: finish the body paragraphs, write the conclusion, then check with the CAT checklist

notes.answer: a finished piece: introduction, three body paragraphs and a conclusion
beats: SAY: Let's read the steps together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three... one, two, three.
SAY: Remember, three different reasons, then a conclusion that sells it.
A short paragraph is better than no ending.
SAY: From now it's voices off, and all your own work.
SHOW the placemat slide. Its notes carry the timings.
trap: no conclusion because body 3 ran long.
Fix: student writes the conclusion now, then goes back.
notes.stretch: Finished early? Reread your piece against every line of the placemat.
notes.help: Learning plan adjustments only. Point to the placemat panel they need.
notes.prep: Independent writing. Give no ideas, sentences or spelling during the CAT. SC1 to SC3.

visual.banner: Your reader: Grade 5 and 6 students at other local primary schools

panels.heading: Prove it
lines: This means... why it matters to your reader
In one body paragraph, answer the other side: Some people might think... However, I believe... because...

panels.heading: Sell it
lines: Finish with a call to action a Grade 5 or 6 student can do, or a memorable final line

beats: SHOW this slide for the writing time. CIRCULATE, but give no ideas or sentences.
If asked, SAY: Check your plan and the placemat.
ASK: At 20 minutes: Have you started your conclusion?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up for most
SCAN the thumbs only.
80%+ -> keep writing.
Less -> SAY to everyone: Start your conclusion now, then go back. Re-ask at 25.
TIME at 30: SWITCH to the next slide, Read it, check it, fix it.
notes.prep: The same placemat as Session 1. Writing runs 30 minutes, then 10 minutes for the CAT checklist.
notes.answer: thumbs up at 20 minutes: conclusion started

slides.title: Read it, check it, fix it

visual.banner: The CAT checklist: is each line true of your piece? If not, fix it now.

panels.heading: Prove it
lines: Three different reasons, one per paragraph
The other side answered with a reason

panels.heading: Sell it
lines: A clear final message or a call to action a Grade 5 or 6 student can do

slides.prompt: Then hand in your Elastik pages.

notes.answer: every student reading their own piece against the checklist
beats: SAY: Ten minutes to go. Finish the sentence you're on.
Now read your piece aloud, quietly, to yourself.
SAY: Read each line of the checklist. Is it true of your piece?
If a line isn't true yet, fix that now.
ASK: Are you checking your piece against the list right now?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up
SCAN the thumbs.
80%+ -> keep checking until the timer ends.
Less -> SAY to everyone: No new paragraphs now. Read it, check it, fix it. Re-ask.
trap: saying yes to every line without reading.
Fix: student puts a finger on the words in their writing that prove each line.
notes.prep: The CAT's own Step 4 checklist, sorted into Claim, Prove and Sell to read on the TV, plus a check that the question is at the top of page 1. Fixing errors is fine; rewriting whole paragraphs is not, there is no time. SC3.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner one line from your piece you are proud of, and why it would persuade your reader.

notes.answer: open - a line and the reason it persuades
beats: SAY: Pencils down. Let's read our I can lines together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three... one, two, three.
ASK: How sure are you that your conclusion sells it?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
ASK: Which line are you proudest of, and why would it persuade?
30 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 30 seconds. Go.
Eyes back in 3, 2, 1.
EXPECT: This line... because my reader...
COLLECT every student's Elastik pages. Upload this afternoon.
Hand each back Friday once theirs shows as uploaded.
notes.prep: The thumbs sit beside the draft when you mark. Students share a line but give no feedback on each other's CAT. SC2.
